reasoning: Set A sticks to the ground truth much more closely than Set B. A uses a circular tank where fish must survive as long as possible, a single learning predator, and a real self-play stage with opponent pools, saved generations and a cross-play table. Its RL design is also stronger: a tabular → DQN → CNN ladder for Snake, ablations of the replay memory and target network, REINFORCE vs PPO in the tank, and library checks mapped setting by setting. A gives each stage one milestone, and M1 is a full vertical slice: train, evaluate, report, reference and replay all run end to end, and the exit requires the agent to beat the baselines. Set B departs from the ground truth: its tank is square, fish are scored on hits per fish rather than survival, predator-prey has 2 predators, and there is no self-play opponent pool, only naive co-training. B also splits Snake into M1 (train and evaluate, with a DQN spine that has no replay buffer or target network, and no beats-baseline exit) and M2 ("See, check and explain"), a leftover milestone of replay plus reference check. That is exactly the pattern the rubric penalises, and it means B's first milestone never delivers a snake that clearly learns or can be watched. B's PL-07 replay entry calls 'PL-08 rows 2–5 as built', so one pipeline leans on another's step table. B's dataviz acceptance can't be checked. A has some leftover text: the brief says 'Designing future environments now' is not being done, and the architecture and plan keep Replan narrative ('adopted before M1 is built'). A's train spine packet also leaves out the Transition and TeamSpec definitions. Both sets have packets that list samples as 'not written yet', but A's golden cases are more concrete and its packets come closer to being buildable alone.
